text:
Chandler Stephenson has 13 points in 16 games, 11 of them assists, and on the surface he looks like a second-line center doing his job in Seattle. Underneath, the 5v5 numbers are the worst on this list: with him on the ice the Kraken have 39% of shot attempts and 39% of expected goals, almost nine points worse than when he sits.

That is not new. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with opponents getting far more chances with him on the ice (bottom 1% of forwards), though they also note he played with weak teammates, which drags his raw numbers down.

The offense comes in transition: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 56% of his shots coming off the rush. He shoots rarely (13 shots) and his points-per-60 is running above his usual range, which suggests the assist pace will slow.

The two-time Stanley Cup winner (Washington and Vegas) still plays 17 and a half minutes a night. Whether that holds if the shot share does not improve is the thing to watch.
headline: Stephenson's assists hide a 5v5 problem
